rows.back_translation: When dawn breaks, Lake Tana awakens in silence. Ethiopia's largest lake, the source of the Abay (Nile).
For ages, tankwa paddlers have lived traveling on this water. The lake is both their road and their dwelling place.
But amidst the forest of the islands, ancient monasteries with a history spanning centuries are hidden.
On their walls, saints appear as brightly colored paintings. Every painting is both a prayer and a lesson.
Books written on parchment have preserved ancient knowledge and faith for centuries.
Writing text on parchment by candle light shows the patience and wisdom of ancient scribes. It is a work that amazes even to this day.
In times of war and hardship, these heritage relics were preserved inside the islands. Even the storm could not destroy them.
Today this trust is in our hands. Knowing, honoring, and protecting it is our share.
Tana is not just a beautiful lake. Since it is a history not destroyed by the storm, let us protect it for the coming generation.
